newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds dip with Treasuries after data.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds dip with Treasuries after data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities gave ground Friday, particularly in mid-level coupons, market experts said.
Most players drifted to the sidelines as Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meetings drew nearer, traders said.
"There were sellers mid-curve, but everything else was pretty quiet," said a Ginnie Mae trader in New York.
Pass-throughs were off 7/32 to 12/32 overall late Friday afternoon, and spreads over Treasuries were unchanged to modestly wider, traders said.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 9/32 at 99-8/32 to yield 106 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 11/32 at 99-8/32 and Freddie Macs were off 10/32 at 99-16/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 9/32 at 6.70 percent.

Earlier, the Commerce Department reported housing starts rose 2.6 percent to an annualized rate of 1.473 million units in April. And the University of Michigan preliminary May index of consumer sentiment was said to be up to a record level of 104.6 from 101.4 in the April final.
